headline: Light rain arrives Saturday night into Sunday, then cool, cloudy, mostly dry weather next week; an active pattern is possible around Halloween.
summary: Skies are mostly clear Friday evening but will turn mostly cloudy overnight as a low-pressure system and front drop south from British Columbia. Overnight lows should reach the mid 30s in the Cascades and nearby foothills and the low 40s around Puget Sound. Rain should reach the coast Saturday afternoon and spread inland Saturday night into Sunday morning, falling mostly on the Olympic Peninsula and west of the Cascades. Amounts vary a lot: the coast and the windward (west-facing) slopes of the Olympics could see up to three quarters of an inch, while the Puget Sound area should get only a few hundredths to a tenth of an inch. Showers taper off late Sunday morning, leaving cloudy skies and highs in the mid to upper 50s. Next week looks cool and cloudy, with the low staying offshore through midweek and highs staying in the mid to upper 50s. A weak disturbance gives a slight chance of light rain from Tuesday afternoon through late Tuesday night, with no more than a few hundredths of an inch expected. Wednesday through Friday look drier as the system moves inland. Forecasters are also watching for a possibly more active pattern from about October 31 to November 6, with only a 20-40% chance of heavier rain, stronger winds and possibly mountain snow; this is far off and uncertain. No watches, warnings, or advisories were in effect for land areas.
changes: Earlier discussions pointed to rain lingering into Monday and a growing chance of below-freezing lows midweek, with unsettled model guidance. By evening, forecasters said the models agreed more, showers end Sunday morning, and next week looks cool and cloudy with only a slight chance of light rain Tuesday. The freezing-lows mention was dropped, and a possibly more active pattern around Halloween and early November was added.
